attributes.readMe:
## Shipment Tracker (ST), Tracking Status View (TV), Feed (Fe)

Three exports, one module, because they read the same event log and must never disagree about it:

- **`TrackingStatusView` (TV)** — the compact stage rail. Four fixed stages, because progress is only legible as a fraction of a known route. A package in exception shows the rail **stalled where it stopped** rather than advancing; a progress bar that keeps moving while nothing happens is a lying affordance.
- **`TrackingEventFeed` (Fe)** — the scan log, oldest first, the way a carrier prints it. Empty is a designed state: no scans in the first few hours is normal, and saying so beats an empty box.
- **`ShipmentTracker` (ST)** — composes both plus the outbound carrier link. Composition rather than a third implementation, so a fix to either half lands in all three consumers.

All three are domain-neutral: they take a status, a list of events and an optional promise, and have no idea what a warehouse is. Anything with scans can mount them.

Events are read property-by-property rather than spread — these are field instances whose values live on prototype accessors that a spread would silently drop.

### Example

Two consumers already: the isolated view of every `Shipment`, and the In transit tab of `OrderFulfilmentApp`, which mounts it in `@compact` mode. `SHP-2026-0142` is the exception case.

### Non-goals

It does not fetch. Scans are handed in; polling a carrier is integration work with no home in the platform yet.
